parallel.requirements: The parent recognized the need for pure Rust 2021, std-only code, root test5.rs, Cargo support, byte-identical output, and CLI argument parsing that ignored extras like the C++ program.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent kept implementation ownership but also spawned probe_binary while it continued work. The child independently took on probing and implementation, with no visible parent-side file ownership or merge contract for shared root outputs.
parallel.implementation: The parent wrote Cargo.toml, test5.rs, and src/ modules using an indicators library with formatting, builder, and tracker logic. The child later wrote a second Cargo.toml and test5.rs plus an indicators/ directory with similar functionality.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The parent copied its built release binary to /output/test5 and later delivered a final answer describing the src/ implementation. The parallel artifact list also contains the child's indicators/ tree and both parent and child build products.
parallel.verification: The parent ran cargo build, cargo test, the release binary, and a reference-output comparison that printed MATCH. The child also ran cargo build, rustc, cargo test, and zero-diff comparisons after its own shared-root writes.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The official solution passed. The remaining process problem is not functional failure but mixed provenance: the child rewrote root deliverables after parent verification and was interrupted before returning a final result to the parent.

serial.requirements: The serial run identified the same Rust 2021, std-only, exact-output, Cargo project, root test5.rs, and CLI argument expectations.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One agent owned the full workflow from probing through implementation, build, standalone compile, output comparison, and final delivery.
serial.implementation: The serial run wrote one Cargo.toml, one test5.rs using #[path = "src/lib.rs"], and src modules for format, progress_builder, and progress_tracker.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial workspace contained a single coherent project layout under /output/src plus root test5.rs and the generated executable /output/test5.
serial.verification: The serial run built with cargo, compiled test5.rs directly to /output/test5, ran both the rustc and Cargo binaries, and diffed /output/test5 against the reference with exit code 0.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unfinished or incorrect task behavior is visible; the official evaluator passed the single testcase.

outcome_analysis.explanation: There is no discordant official outcome: the current completed status evaluation for both modes reports solution_passed true with 1/1 testcases. The concrete task-solving difference is procedural, not result-changing: parallel duplicated full-solution work across parent and child and ended with mixed shared-state provenance, while serial completed one coherent implementation path.
parallel_contributors: Parent implementation produced exact expected output and passed local checks before finalization.
Child produced an additional successful implementation path but rewrote shared root deliverables after parent verification.
serial_contributors: Single agent implemented one project layout and verified /output/test5 against the reference binary.
No child handoff, merge, or shared-write coordination was needed.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel parent used src/formatting.rs and package name indicators, while the child used an indicators/ directory and package name test5; serial used src/format.rs and package name indicators_migration. These layout/name differences did not affect the official pass.
evaluator_effects: Both official evaluator records completed successfully and passed the only testcase, so no evaluator-specific discrepancy explains the pair.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained pattern is an adverse parallel process issue, not a failure cause

The parent assembled and copied an executable, and the child also compiled; final assembly was owned and completed.
The parent drove the end-to-end pipeline through implementation, build, test, comparison, and final response.
Implementation was not blocked behind a mandatory preflight; parent and child proceeded to write code while probing was still active.
Investigation and implementation overlapped; the parent did not defer all productive work until child investigation completed.
The indispensable implementation path was not starved; the parent completed and verified a passing solution before closure.
Only one child is visible and the run completed well within budget; there is no collective fan-out exhaustion.
The child scope was not proven overbroad for the available window, and the child produced buildable code before interruption.
The observable child work addressed the required output, Cargo build, standalone rustc path, and std-only implementation; no known requirement omission caused unusable work.
The agents were not producing separate components meant to interoperate; the concrete failure mode was a same-root deliverable rewrite.
No known finding is shown disappearing through a transfer; the child worked from its own task context and no lossy handoff drove rework.

No receiver consumed stale child or parent handoff information that described a superseded state.

The parent had local build/test/output evidence and the child also verified after its write; there was no visible unresolved functional acceptance gap before closure.
No retry or replacement child repeated prior work without inherited checkpoints; the visible child was the initial spawned child.

The child did write after parent verification, but it was a concrete shared deliverable overwrite and the child then ran its own build/test checks, so the write label is more specific.
The child implementation was not merely completed elsewhere and left unjoined; it directly wrote into the shared output tree.
The child was an implementer, not only a verifier returning a concrete finding that became trapped below the parent.
No required child failure left necessary task scope abandoned; the parent and child both produced passing implementations.
No normal completed child result was returned and then ignored by the parent; the child was interrupted and its writes were already in the shared tree.
The parent waited for the child twice, but it had already finished core verification and the concrete adverse effect is the shared deliverable rewrite rather than waiting displacing required work.
The agents did not merely write different files with overlapping behavior; the child also touched the required root deliverable paths.
Same-file overlap is present, but the affected files include the required root executable source and Cargo configuration, so Deliverable Overwrite is more specific.

candidates.near_match_reason: Although the child wrote after parent verification, this was not a parent merge of a returned child result; the directly observed coordination boundary is the child overwriting shared deliverable files.

retained_patterns.reason: The parent first created and verified the required root deliverables, then a still-running child wrote its own root Cargo.toml and test5.rs in the same output workspace. That concrete shared deliverable rewrite is absent in serial, which used one writer and one coherent project tree.
retained_patterns.realized_consequence: The parallel final artifact carried a mixed, stale-provenance workspace after the child rewrote required root deliverables later than the parent's successful verification, even though the final behavior still passed.
retained_patterns.near_match_reason: The child change was not a parent-controlled merge of a returned result after verification; the specific harmful boundary was direct overwrite of root deliverable paths.

deduplicated_same_label_episodes: The repeated same root paths Cargo.toml and test5.rs are treated as one Deliverable Overwrite episode because they belong to one child rewrite of the shared deliverable set.
suppressed_same_chain_candidates: Same-File Collision, Source Overwrite, Unisolated Workspace Writes, and Merge after Verification are not retained separately because they restate the same child rewrite episode at a less specific or downstream boundary.

Early Child Termination and Blind Timeout Wait are not retained because the child interruption/waiting did not abandon required work; the realized adverse consequence was already captured by the overwrite.
